thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Hosted API p99 latency spike detected in eu-west-1. queue_length=27,400, p95=3.2s, p99=15.1s, error_rate(502)=4.8%. autoscaler errors: provisioner-rate-limit(429)

emma_sre: oncall here. acknowledging. paging ml/oncall and infra. any known deploys? :rotating_light:

raj_ml_oncall: saw the alert. looks like GPU pools are saturated and autoscaler keep retrying new instances but cloud quota is returning 403/429. hitting warmup delays too. I'm jumping in.

alice_infra: checking provisioner logs — we're seeing long create times and many API throttles from cloud provider. snippet:```provisioner: create_instance() -> 429 QuotaExceeded
retry_count=5, backoff=16s
alloc_pool=eu-gpu-highmem
```

ben_prod: we also have a high-volume marketing push from a partner; traffic doubled in 6m and is very bursty (short TTL chat completions). customers hitting timeouts at 10s+. product informed.

jordan_cs: Heads-up: two enterprise customers reported failed requests and are escalating. collecting request ids for support.

emma_sre: immediate mitigations: 1) enable rate-limit policy for new campaign routes to 20req/min 2) enable fallback routing to smaller quantized model (cpu/dedicated-quant4) for non-SLAs 3) pause noncritical batch jobs to free GPUs

emma_sre: applying rate limit...
ops-bot: /config apply-rate-limit --route "/v1/generate/campaign/*" --limit 20rpm --actor emergency
ops-bot: rate-limit applied to 2 routes (eu-west-1).

raj_ml_oncall: enabling fallback model route: endpoint -> model:redwood-quant4-small (cpu-backed). This will increase latency on some tokens but prevents timeouts.
ops-bot: /routes set-fallback --from model:large-gpu --to model:redwood-quant4-small --threshold queue>2000
ops-bot: fallback activated for 3 shards.

alice_infra: autoscaler logs show leader election slow; provisioner stuck on exponential backoff due to 429s. Suggest temporary override to bump reserved capacity (if we have quota) or spin up preemptible GPU capacity in another AZ and route traffic.

ben_prod: can we spin up our Dedicated pool capacity in eu-west as emergency instead of cloud provisioner? We have some reserved infra there.

emma_sre: raj, can you confirm compatibility of requests with dedicated pool (kv cache, sess tokens)?

raj_ml_oncall: quick check: majority of campaign traffic is stateless completion calls — compatible. I'll flip routing rules to send 25% of campaign traffic to dedicated pool as a circuit-breaker.
ops-bot: /routing set-weight --route "/v1/generate/campaign/*" --backend dedicated-eu-02 --weight 25%
ops-bot: routing updated.

alice_infra: spun up 4 preemptible gpus in eu-west-2 and updated provisioner. new nodes appear but warmup still taking ~45s each due to container pull + model load.

emma_sre: rolling telemetry: queue dropped from 27.4k -> 9.8k after rate-limit + fallback + 25% diversion. p95 -> 1.1s, p99 -> 4.2s. error_rate down to 1.6%. still above baseline but improving.

jordan_cs: informing customers with a brief status update and ETA for stabilization.

ben_prod: note: autoscaler team to follow up on quota issue with cloud rep. need to avoid relying on last-minute preemptible spins for future.

raj_ml_oncall: final tweak: reduce model max_seq to 512 for campaign routes to shave token compute and reduce GPU memory pressure. ops-bot applied config.
ops-bot: /models update --model large-gpu --max_seq 512 --scope "/v1/generate/campaign/*"

emma_sre: status check 12m after initial alert: queue ~1.2k, p95=210ms, p99=780ms, error_rate 0.3%. Stabilizing. I'll keep the incident channel open for 1h for postmortem notes. If anything regresses, page SRE.

alice_infra: opened ticket INFRA-9071 to track cloud quota, autoscaler backoff logic, and faster warmup images.

ben_prod: opened PROD-3388 to review routing policies and campaign safe-guarding (scheduled rate caps for known partners).

emma_sre: incident classified as Sev2. Initial cause: sudden ad/campaign fanout -> GPU pool saturation + cloud quota-induced autoscaler backoff -> warmup lag -> request queue growth -> timeouts. Mitigations: rate-limits, fallback to quantized model, partial diversion to Dedicated pool, temp preemptible capacity, model max_seq cap.

jordan_cs: customers updated. Escalation channel closed. Postmortem owner: emma_sre. Link to postmortem will be posted in #eng-postmortems when ready. :white_check_mark:
